# Closure and Escalation Notes

**PowerShell Execution With Encoded Command** · `T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command` · [T1059.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     Image=<value>  OriginalFileName=<value>  CommandLine=<value>  ParentImage=<value>
Checked:      1. Decode the Base64 blob (UTF-16LE) and read the script -> <result>
              2. Check the parent process -> <result>
              3. Search 4104 script blocks on the same host and time -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | sccm_client (applied)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Management agents (SCCM, Intune, RMM tools) that use encoded commands
- Ansible's WinRM bootstrap, an -EncodedCommand started by cmd /C on every managed host (public data: the labs' provisioning)

Never tune:
- Never filter by the Base64 content alone: the same payload can be re-encoded trivially. A reviewed automation bootstrap is excepted only by its source host together with its exact command line.
- Never filter Office, browser or script-host parents: they are the delivery path this rule exists for.

```text

Who / where:  <account> on <host>; source <host or address, if any>
Risk:         base 40 + <conditions met> = <score>
Preserved:    Full command line and decoded script -> <where it is saved>
              4104 script blocks -> <where it is saved>
              Parent process tree -> <where it is saved>
              Network connections and DNS queries from the process -> <where it is saved>
Containment:  none yet | <action taken, time UTC>
Recommended:  Block contacted infrastructure, remove persistence created by the script, isolate the host if a second stage ran
```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. Parent is Office, a browser, wscript, mshta or an unknown binary
2. Decoded script downloads content or uses IEX
3. Network connections from the PowerShell process (Sysmon EID 3)

Risk conditions: suspicious parent +25 · host is critical +15 · user is privileged +10 · outside business hours +10 · known vendor software -25 · approved admin activity -20.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Block the remote host or domain seen in the script
2. Isolate the host if a second stage executed
3. Remove any persistence created by the script
